blocks.x: CLINICAL INDICATION:
[Acute colicky abdominal pain / Bloody stools / Rule out intussusception.]
TECHNIQUE:
Targeted high-frequency linear and general curvilinear grayscale and color Doppler ultrasound of the gastrointestinal tract, solid abdominal organs, and pelvis.
FINDINGS:
Bowel / Gastrointestinal (Primary Finding):

In the [right lower quadrant / right upper quadrant / subhepatic region], there is a concentric, multilayered bowel-within-bowel mass demonstrating a classic "target sign" in the transverse plane and "pseudokidney sign" longitudinally, measuring [X.X] x [X.X] cm in outer-to-outer transverse diameter and [X.X] cm in length, consistent with an ileocolic intussusception.
Vascularity: Color and power Doppler interrogation demonstrates preserved intramural blood flow within both the intussusceptum and intussuscipiens [or: diminished/absent internal flow].
Interloop Fluid: No trapped interloop fluid is identified within the intussusceptum [or: Small pocket of trapped anechoic interloop fluid is present].

Lead Point / Nodes: Multiple enlarged, oval hypoechoic mesenteric lymph nodes (up to [X.X] cm) and echogenic mesenteric fat are incorporated within the intussusceptum; no discrete solid or cystic pathologic lead point is seen.
Bowel Caliber: [Mildly dilated, fluid-filled proximal small bowel loops with hyperperistalsis / No upstream small bowel dilatation to suggest mechanical obstruction].
Peritoneum:
Trace simple anechoic free fluid in the [right iliac fossa / pelvis]. No complex/echogenic free fluid or free intraperitoneal air.
Abbreviated Survey of Remaining Organs:
Liver, Gallbladder & Biliary Tree: Normal hepatic size and homogeneous echotexture without focal lesion. Gallbladder is thin-walled and anechoic without stones or biliary dilatation.
Pancreas & Spleen: Visualized pancreas is unremarkable. Spleen is normal in size and homogeneous in echotexture.
Kidneys & Bladder: Normal bilateral renal size and cortical echogenicity without hydronephrosis. Urinary bladder is unremarkable.
Pelvis: [Uterus and bilateral ovaries appear normal for age / Unremarkable male pelvic structures].
IMPRESSION:

Ileocolic intussusception in the [right lower / right upper] quadrant measuring [X.X] cm in transverse diameter, with [preserved / diminished] internal Doppler vascularity and [no / present] trapped interloop fluid.
[Trace simple free peritoneal fluid and reactive mesenteric lymphadenopathy.]
Urgent pediatric surgical consultation for image-guided [pneumatic / hydrostatic] enema reduction is recommended.
CLINICAL INDICATION:
[Acute abdominal pain / Rule out intussusception / Rule out acute appendicitis.]
TECHNIQUE:

Real-time grayscale and color Doppler sonographic evaluation of the solid abdominal organs, retroperitoneum, pelvic organs, and gastrointestinal tract was performed using curvilinear and high-frequency linear transducers.
FINDINGS:
Liver:

Normal in size (measuring [X.X] cm in the midclavicular line) with smooth contours and homogeneous parenchymal echogenicity. No focal solid or cystic mass is identified. The portal vein is patent with normal hepatopetal flow.
Gallbladder & Biliary Tree:

The gallbladder is physiologically distended with an anechoic lumen, normal wall thickness (less than 3 mm), and no gallstones, sludge, or pericholecystic fluid. Negative sonographic Murphy sign. No intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation (CBD measures [X.X] mm).
Pancreas:
Visualized portions of the pancreatic head, body, and tail appear normal in size and homogeneous in echotexture without focal lesion or pancreatic duct dilatation.
Spleen:
Normal in size (measuring [X.X] cm in length) with uniform parenchymal echogenicity and no focal lesion.
Kidneys & Urinary Bladder:

Both kidneys are normal in size, position, and cortical echogenicity with preserved corticomedullary differentiation (right kidney [X.X] cm, left kidney [X.X] cm). No hydronephrosis, nephrolithiasis, or focal mass.
The urinary bladder is adequately distended with smooth, regular walls and anechoic lumen.
Bowel / Gastrointestinal:
Survey of the small and large bowel demonstrates normal bowel wall thickness (less than 3 mm), normal compressibility, and preserved peristalsis throughout.
No concentric bowel-within-bowel configuration, "target sign," or "pseudokidney sign" is identified to suggest intussusception.
No dilated, fluid-filled bowel loops to suggest mechanical bowel obstruction.
Graded-compression evaluation of the right lower quadrant shows no blind-ending, non-compressible tubular structure or surrounding inflammatory fat stranding to suggest acute appendicitis.
Pelvis & Peritoneum:
[For Female Patients:] The uterus is normal in size and myometrial echotexture with a thin, regular endometrial stripe. Both ovaries are normal in size and appearance with normal Doppler vascularity.
[For Male Patients:] The prostate gland and seminal vesicles appear unremarkable for age.
No free intraperitoneal fluid, complex collections, or free intraperitoneal air. No pathologically enlarged retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymph nodes.
IMPRESSION:
Normal abdominopelvic ultrasound.
No sonographic evidence of intussusception, acute appendicitis, or bowel obstruction.

bank.title: PART 1: HOW THE REPORT IS STRUCTURED
items: Professional radiologists almost always evaluate and report intussusception as part of a comprehensive Abdominopelvic Ultrasound, rather than as an isolated, standalone bowel-only exam.

Even when a clinician orders a "targeted bowel ultrasound" to rule out intussusception, standard radiology practice (including ACR and pediatric radiology guidelines) requires scanning the solid organs and pelvis. This is done to exclude common clinical mimics (such as appendicitis, mesenteric adenitis, ovarian torsion, or renal colic) and to check for secondary complications like free fluid or a pathologic lead point.
Depending on the department's PACS/RIS macros, radiologists organize the report in one of two ways:

Dedicated "Bowel / Gastrointestinal" Subheading (Most Common): Placed within the standard abdominopelvic template right after the solid organs (liver, gallbladder, pancreas, spleen, kidneys) and before free fluid/pelvis.

Prominent Lead in "Findings" + Abbreviated Normal Organ Survey: In acute pediatric emergencies, the radiologist puts the positive intussusception block first so the emergency team sees it immediately, followed by brief normal lines for the remaining abdominal organs.

bank.title: PART 2: KEY ELEMENTS RADIOLOGISTS DOCUMENT

subs.title: Classic Sonographic Signs & Dimensions
items: Transverse view: "Target sign" or "doughnut sign" (alternating concentric hyperechoic mucosal/mesenteric and hypoechoic muscularis layers).
Longitudinal view: "Pseudokidney sign" or "sandwich sign".

Measurements: Outer-to-outer transverse diameter (typically greater than 2.5 cm for ileocolic intussusception; small bowel–to–small bowel is usually smaller and often transient) and approximate craniocaudal length.

subs.title: Anatomical Location & Type
items: Quadrant/region (most commonly the right lower quadrant or right upper quadrant subhepatic space).
Classification: Ileocolic (requires reduction) versus ileoileal / small bowel (often transient and self-limiting if short and without a lead point).

subs.title: Vascularity & Viability (Prognostic Red Flags)
items: Color Doppler: Presence or absence of intramural blood flow within the intussusceptum. Absent flow raises concern for bowel ischemia/necrosis and lowers the threshold for surgical vs. enema management.
Trapped Fluid: Presence of trapped interloop fluid within the intussusceptum (associated with lower enema reduction success rates and higher ischemia risk).

subs.title: Pathologic Lead Points (PLPs) & Associated Findings
items: Assessment for focal masses inside the intussusceptum (e.g., Meckel diverticulum, duplication cyst, polyp, lymphoma, or hypertrophied Peyer patches/mesenteric lymph nodes).
Small bowel obstruction: Proximal dilated, fluid-filled bowel loops with hyperperistalsis or to-and-fro motion.
Free fluid: Simple vs. complex/echogenic peritoneal fluid (echogenic fluid or pneumoperitoneum flags perforation, an absolute contraindication to enema reduction).
To guide the surgeon or radiologist performing an enema reduction (air or hydrostatic), a complete intussusception report goes beyond simply stating that a mass is present. It systematically covers:

bank.title: PART 3: MODULAR DIAGNOSTIC PHRASE BANK
items: Here is a modular diagnostic phrase bank structured for rapid insertion into an Abdominopelvic Ultrasound report template. Each block is organized by anatomical/diagnostic sub-category so you can mix and match findings seamlessly.

bank.title: 1. Primary Intussusception Findings (Insert under Bowel / Gastrointestinal)

subs.title: Classic Ileocolic Intussusception (Standard Positive)
items: In the [right lower quadrant / right upper quadrant / subhepatic region], there is a concentric, multilayered bowel-within-bowel mass demonstrating a classic "target sign" in the transverse plane and "pseudokidney sign" longitudinally, measuring [X.X] x [X.X] cm in outer-to-outer transverse diameter and [X.X] cm in length, consistent with an ileocolic intussusception.

subs.title: Transient / Small Bowel (Ileoileal) Intussusception
items: In the [periumbilical region / left abdomen / right lower quadrant], there is a short-segment, small-caliber bowel-within-bowel configuration measuring [X.X] cm in transverse diameter (less than 2.0 cm) and [X.X] cm in length, lacking significant mesenteric fat invagination. Spontaneous reduction was observed during real-time scanning [or: findings are characteristic of a transient small bowel intussusception; clinical correlation is advised].

subs.title: Post-Reduction / Residual Edema
items: Following successful [hydrostatic / pneumatic] enema reduction, the previously noted intussusception has resolved. Residual circumferential hypoechoic wall thickening of the terminal ileum and ileocecal valve is noted, consistent with post-reduction mucosal edema.

bank.title: 2. Doppler Viability & Prognostic Indicators (Sub-bullets under Intussusception)

subs.title: Preserved Vascularity (Favorable for Enema Reduction)
items: Vascularity: Color and power Doppler interrogation demonstrates preserved intramural blood flow within both the intussusceptum and intussuscipiens.

subs.title: Diminished / Absent Vascularity (High Ischemia Risk)
items: Vascularity: Color Doppler demonstrates markedly diminished [or: absent] internal vascular flow within the intussusceptum, raising concern for bowel wall ischemia/compromise.

subs.title: Trapped Interloop Fluid
items: Interloop Fluid: A small [or: moderate] pocket of trapped anechoic fluid is present between the serosal surfaces of the invaginated bowel loops within the intussusceptum (associated with increased risk of ischemia and lower hydrostatic/pneumatic reduction success).
No Interloop Fluid: No trapped interloop fluid is identified within the intussusceptum.

subs.title: Reactive Lymphoid Hyperplasia (Idiopathic / Most Common)
items: Lead Point / Nodes: Multiple enlarged, oval hypoechoic mesenteric lymph nodes (measuring up to [X.X] cm in short axis) are dragged into the intussusceptum alongside invaginated echogenic mesenteric fat; no discrete solid or cystic pathologic lead point is identified.

subs.title: Suspected Pathologic Lead Point
items: Lead Point: Within the apex of the intussusceptum, there is a well-defined [cystic / solid / polypoid] lesion measuring [X.X] x [X.X] cm, suspicious for a pathologic lead point (such as a [Meckel diverticulum / enteric duplication cyst / juvenile polyp / lymphoma]).

subs.title: Indeterminate / Obscured Apex
items: Lead Point: Evaluation of the intussusceptum apex for an underlying pathologic lead point is limited by overlying bowel gas and acoustic shadowing; post-reduction reassessment is recommended.

subs.title: Proximal Small Bowel Obstruction (SBO)
items: Bowel Caliber: Fluid-filled, dilated proximal small bowel loops (measuring up to [X.X] cm in diameter) are present with hyperperistalsis [or: sluggish to-and-fro peristalsis], consistent with secondary mechanical small bowel obstruction.

subs.title: Normal Proximal Bowel
items: Bowel Caliber: No significant upstream small bowel dilatation or sonographic evidence of high-grade mechanical bowel obstruction.

subs.title: Peritoneal Free Fluid (Simple vs. Complex)
items: Peritoneum (Simple): Trace [or: small] simple anechoic free fluid is noted in the right iliac fossa and pelvis. No free intraperitoneal air.

Peritoneum (Complex / Perforation Alert): Moderate complex, echogenic free peritoneal fluid containing low-level internal debris is present in the pelvis and right paracolic gutter, concerning for bowel wall compromise or perforation (an absolute contraindication to enema reduction).

subs.title: Targeted Rule-Out (Clean Negative)
items: Bowel / Gastrointestinal: No bowel-within-bowel configuration, "target sign," or "pseudokidney sign" is identified to suggest intussusception. Bowel loops demonstrate normal wall thickness, compressibility, and active peristalsis.

subs.title: Comprehensive Pediatric Acute Abdomen Rule-Out
items: Bowel / Gastrointestinal: No sonographic evidence of intussusception. The appendix is visualized in the right lower quadrant, measuring [X.X] mm in maximal outer diameter, fully compressible with no surrounding echogenic fat stranding or hyperemia. Scattered non-enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes are noted.

subs.title: Suboptimal / Gas-Limited Rule-Out
items: Bowel / Gastrointestinal: No sonographic evidence of intussusception is seen within the visualized bowel segments; however, evaluation of the deep right lower quadrant and retrocecal region is partially limited by overlying intraluminal bowel gas. If clinical suspicion remains high, continued clinical observation or repeat sonography is advised.

subs.title: Uncomplicated Ileocolic Intussusception
items: Ileocolic intussusception in the [right lower / right upper] quadrant measuring [X.X] cm in transverse diameter, with preserved internal Doppler vascularity and no trapped interloop fluid or free air to suggest ischemia or perforation.
Urgent pediatric surgical consultation for image-guided [pneumatic / hydrostatic] enema reduction is recommended.

subs.title: Complicated / High-Risk Intussusception
items: Ileocolic intussusception in the [right lower / right upper] quadrant measuring [X.X] cm in transverse diameter, complicated by [absent internal Doppler vascularity / trapped interloop fluid / complex free peritoneal fluid / secondary small bowel obstruction], raising high concern for bowel ischemia [or perforation].
Immediate pediatric surgical evaluation is recommended prior to any attempt at enema reduction.

subs.title: Negative Study
items: No sonographic evidence of intussusception or acute appendicitis. Normal abdominopelvic ultrasound.
